agree.reason: The landlord gets clear, firm terms and a straight answer on the late payments and the coffee chain, but nothing puts a dollar figure on what a vacancy would cost him, so he has little reason to drop $550 a month.

honest.reason: Every number traces back to the brief or to what the user knows, and the only stretch is the confident line that a coffee shop 'has little use' for the hood, which is a reasonable guess but still a guess.

works_the_facts.reason: The year-five figure of about $5,740 is correct and useful because it beats his $5,650 ask, but the letter never works out the per-square-foot rate of the offer (about $26), the rent he lost on the 14-month vacancy, or the five-year total.

right_comparison.reason: It mentions the unit that has sat empty for 14 months at $28, but it never says that his ask works out to about $29, more than the price that hasn't found a tenant, so the strongest comparison is left out.

qualification.reason: Asking for an answer by June 1 with the August lease end as the reason is concrete and easy to check, though the letter doesn't say what happens if that date passes.

objections.reason: It deals well with the late payments (the cooler failure, autopay going forward) and with the coffee chain, but bringing up the 6% sales drop hands a wary landlord a fresh reason to doubt the restaurant can keep paying.

fit.reason: It's a short, polite email of about 300 words, as the brief asked, but it's signed only 'Pho Lan' instead of the owner's name.
